page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-metal is a bare-metal server configured with 288 dedicated vCPUs across 144 physical cores, utilizing Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors running at 4.2 GHz. The system features 1080.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is also in the top 10%, reaching 23040.71 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 1087.82 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The server excels in database operations, achieving 40009.67 operations on PassMark and 413.48 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks.

While the server demonstrates strong performance in medium and large LLM prompt processing, text generation for small 135M models is poor, falling into the bottom 10% at 42.44 tokens/sec. Additionally, the complete absence of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage options, which may impact I/O-heavy workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this bare-metal instance offers high resource density for compute-heavy, non-GPU workloads. It is suited for multi-threaded CPU tasks, large-scale database hosting, software compilation, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
